sources.entry: pytorch-lightning - Deep learning framework to train, deploy, and ship AI products Lightning fast.

summary.one_liner: PyTorch Lightning is a deep learning framework that organizes PyTorch training code to automate engineering tasks such as multi-GPU, distributed, and mixed-precision training while keeping model logic in plain PyTorch.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes two packages: PyTorch Lightning, which wraps a LightningModule and a Trainer to handle the training loop, and Lightning Fabric, which gives expert-level control over the PyTorch loop and scaling strategy with fewer abstractions. Users define training_step and configure_optimizers, then call Trainer.fit. The Trainer options cover devices, number of nodes, TPUs, and 16-bit precision without changing model code. It includes callbacks such as EarlyStopping and ModelCheckpoint, and loggers for TensorBoard, Weights and Biases, Comet, MLflow, and LitLogger. Models can be exported to TorchScript or ONNX. Fabric supports DDP, FSDP, and DeepSpeed strategies. The README also lists example tasks such as image classification, segmentation, object detection, text classification, LLM finetuning, and time-series forecasting.
use_cases: Train a PyTorch model on multiple GPUs without rewriting code
Finetune a pretrained image or text model
Scale PyTorch training across multi-node clusters
Add checkpointing and early stopping to a training run
Export a trained PyTorch model to TorchScript or ONNX
Build a custom training loop with expert-level control
how_to_run: Define a LightningModule with training_step and configure_optimizers
Create data loaders for training and validation
notable: Lightning Fabric offers lower-level control, letting users write a custom Trainer from its primitives
Same code runs on CPU, GPU, TPU, or multi-node setups by changing Trainer arguments
Built-in export to TorchScript and ONNX
caveats: The README states Lightning Cloud offers GPUs and a free tier, but its paid tiers are not described
The README claims about 300 ms per-epoch overhead compared with pure PyTorch, which is a stated figure rather than a benchmark
The CI status table in the README has no visible results, so current test status is unclear
